The *Kāḷigodhāputtabhaddiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 45) is a poetic biographical narrative located in the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
Computational text-reuse data from DharmaNexus indicates extensive overlap between this text and later Pali commentarial literature, most notably the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (both the Dutiyo and Paṭhamo bhāgo), where almost the entire text (§§1.1–15.4) is cited or shared [DharmaNexus]. Within the Therāpadāna itself, formulaic verse segments are shared with several other elders' apadānas, including the *Bhāgineyyupālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 43), *Tissametteyyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 403), *Cundattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 52), *Udenattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 412), *Mahāmoggallānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 4), and *Ānandattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 12) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also identifies automated cross-language alignments with the Tibetan translations of the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka* (D0056) and *Lalitavistara* (D0095), as well as the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
